<!--
    Please give your PR a title in the form "area: short description".  For example "tsdb: reduce disk usage by 95%"

    If your PR is to fix an issue, put "Fixes #issue-number" in the description.

    Don't forget!

    - Please sign CNCF's Developer Certificate of Origin and sign-off your commits by adding the -s / --signoff flag to `git commit`. See https://github.com/apps/dco for more information.

    - If the PR adds or changes a behaviour or fixes a bug of an exported API it would need a unit/e2e test.

    - Where possible use only exported APIs for tests to simplify the review and make it as close as possible to an actual library usage.

    - Performance improvements would need a benchmark test to prove it.

    - All exposed objects should have a comment.

    - All comments should start with a capital letter and end with a full stop.
 -->

Fixes: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/11618 https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/8086

The RO head could alter the mmap chunks while replaying the WAL e.g. https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/e6d3d6abd99d1eda8576809b62d59d606ee1d5ac/tsdb/head_wal.go#L594

The other possibility is if it tries to repair a chunk file in repairLastChunkFile or when adjusting corrupted chunks.

---

This PR:

chore(tsdb): add a sandboxDir to DBReadOnly, the directory can be used for transient file writes.
    
use it in loadDataAsQueryable to make sure the RO Head doesn't truncate or cut new chunks in data/chunks_head/.
    
add a -sandbox-dir-root flag to "promtool tsdb dump/dump-openmetrics" to control the root of that sandbox dirrectory.

---

~- [ ] put "feature behind a flag"~
- [x] allow setting the tmp path (to be able to use a FS with enough space if needed etc.)
- [ ] doc that extra disk space may be needed

### What did you do?

Prometheus 2.39.1, on FreeBSD 13.1

Not sure exactly what triggered this, prometheus have been running happily on this machine since ages. Upgraded from 2.36.0 on nov 8 and have been running fine since.

Yesterday I ran some 'promtool tsdb dump' commands, which to my knowledge should not affect running instance.
I also placed an empty file in the DB directory (arbitrary.txt).
Quote soon after this, it had a first panic. At first I thought it could be that file interfering, so removed that and restarted prometheus.
~2 hrs later, it crashed again with similar error. At that point in time I was asleep, and could not restart the process until way later (sometimes I miss systemd...)

comments: cc @jesusvazquez can this be related to ooo?
Could you try 2.37 (Prometheus LTS) and see if the issue happens here too?

I need to reproduce the error but a couple of early thoughts.

> cc @jesusvazquez can this be related to ooo?

I don't think so since out-of-order is not enabled in the configuration but I will not discard it until we've found the root cause.

> Yesterday I ran some 'promtool tsdb dump' commands, which to my knowledge should not affect running instance.

I went to look at the promtool tsdb dump command and I found that when the new head in read only mode is created, a chunk disk mapper is instantiated and part of the process is memory mapping available chunk files on disk, part of that is actually repairing the last chunk file https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/3330d85ba8cd6c53e74af23ab96e9e2c134bec39/tsdb/chunks/head_chunks.go#L294-L297 so it can potentially modify the TSDB.

I would have guessed that `promtool tsdb dump` doesn't do anything but it can actually lead into a race condition if the tsdb is dumped before samples are written into the chunk.

Also if the `promtool` command version is old it may initialize an old head that can't really do things such as processing the write behind log (added by out-of-order in 2.39.0) or reading out of order chunks. I don't think this can be an issue here because you were upgrading your version and you probably did not ingest ooo samples since it was not enabled but this is a mental note for the future where we might want to warn the user about updating `promtool` to the version of the head that it is reading.

> Nov 22 22:00:03 back-1 prometheus[3729]: panic: expected newly cut file to have sequence:offset 10613:8, got 10617:8

This is what is getting my attention now. Chunk references grow 1 by 1 and the error here is pointing out that we expected to write `10613` but we found that the last chunk on disk was `10617`. This leads me to think that something else was creating chunks and I don't understand what was it.

I believe the chunkdiskmapper implementation also changed between 2.36.0 and 2.39.1 so I'll investigate that next.

This is easy to reproduce:

Just run a Prometheus instance with:

```
global:
  scrape_interval:     1s

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: prometheus
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['localhost:9090']
```

And a dump in a loop:

```
while true; do clear && ./promtool tsdb dump data/ && sleep 1; done;
```
and wait for the panic to happen.

Because we cannot prevent (it'll be difficult to prevent) the RO head from going the mmaping path, which may result in some writes, while loading the WAL, we can try to contain it by granting the RO head its own MmappedChunksDir (different head, different mapped files). We could put hardlinks to the original immutable chunks in there to avoid recreating them.

I have a PoC of that here: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/13218

Your input is welcome.
